detail: Basalt is often dark gray to black in color due to its high concentration of augite or other dark-colored pyroxene minerals, but it can vary greatly in shade. Basalt's physical attributes reflect its comparatively low silica content and high iron and magnesium content. Basalt makes up more than 90% of all volcanic rock on Earth, and it is also found on other planets in the solar system.
application:
Basalt is used in construction for building blocks, interior and exterior walls, floors, worktops, sinks, monuments, pool coping, sills, paving stone, stepping stone, cobblestones, and statues. Heating and extruding basalt produces stone wool, which has the potential to be a great thermal insulator. Basalt turns into metamorphic rock counterparts when subjected to intense heat or pressure. Basalt natural stone is also found on the surface of Mars, the Moon, Venus, and the asteroid Vesta. Basalt makes up a major portion of the earth's crust and can also be found throughout the solar system.

Basalt outcrops weather more quickly than granitic rocks exposed on the earth's surface. This reflects their mineral makeup, which crystallized at greater temperatures and in a less water-vapor-rich environment than granite. These minerals are less stable under the cooler, wetter conditions found at the earth's surface. Basalt is the most prevalent volcanic rock type, accounting for more than 90% of all volcanic rock on the world. The crustal parts of oceanic tectonic plates are primarily made of basalt, which is formed from upwelling mantle beneath ocean ridges. Basalt is also the primary volcanic rock on many marine islands.

name: Natural Indian Soapstone
summary: Soapstone is a talc-schist, which is a type of metamorphic rock, it is composed largely of the magnesium rich mineral talc. It is produced by dynamothermal metamorphism and metasom
detail: Soapstone is a talc-schist, which is a type of metamorphic rock, it is composed largely of the magnesium rich mineral talc. It is produced by dynamothermal metamorphism and metasomatism, which occur in the zones where tectonic plates are subducted, changing rocks by heat and pressure, with influx of fluids, but without melting. It has been a medium for carving and sculptures for thousands of years.
application:
Soapstone is relatively soft because of its high talc content, softer grades may feel similar to soap when touched, hence the name. No fixed hardness is given for soapstone because the amount of talc it contains varies widely, from as little as 30% for architectural grades such as those used on countertops, to as much as 80% for carving grades. the abundance of soapstone mines allow local artisans to craft pots, pans, wine glasses, statues, jewel boxes, coasters and vases. Soapstones can be put in a freezer and later used in place of ice cubes to chill alcoholic beverages without diluting, sometimes called whiskey stones.

In modern times, soapstone is most commonly used for architectural applications, such as counter tops, floor tiles, bathroom tiling, showerbases, and interior surfacing because of the ease of working the material and its property. Soapstone is sometimes used for construction of fireplace surrounds, cladding on wood-burning stoves, and as the preferred material for woodburning masonry heaters because it can absorb, store, and evenly radiate heat due to its high density and magnesite content. Soapstone is easy to carve; it is also durable, heat-resistant and has a high heat storage capacity.

name: Indian Travertine Stone
summary: Travertine is a sedimentary rock formed by the chemical precipitation of calcium carbonate minerals from fresh water, typically in springs, rivers and lakes; from surface and groun
detail: Travertine is a sedimentary rock formed by the chemical precipitation of calcium carbonate minerals from fresh water, typically in springs, rivers and lakes; from surface and ground waters. Travertine includes deposits in both hot and cold springs, including the porous, spongy rock. It often has a fibrous or concentric appearance and exists in white, ivory, tan, cream-colored and even rusty varieties.
application:
Travertine is one of the most frequently used stones in modern architecture. It is commonly used for indoor home/business flooring, outdoor patio flooring, spa walls and ceilings, façades, and wall cladding, building stone, ornamental stone, countertops, monuments, pool coping, sills, paving stone. It typically lacks planes of weakness, and its high porosity makes it light in weight for its strength, gives it good thermal and acoustic insulating properties and makes it relatively easy to work. Dense travertine makes excellent decorative stone when polished. Italy had a near-monopoly on the world travertine market; now significant supplies are quarried in Turkey, Mexico, China, Peru, Spain and India.

Travertine is one of several natural stones that are used for paving patios and garden paths. It is sometimes known as travertine limestone or travertine marble; these are the same stone, although travertine is classified properly as a type of limestone, not marble. The stone is characterised by pitted holes and troughs in its surface. Although these troughs occur naturally, they suggest signs of considerable wear and tear over time. It can also be polished to a smooth, shiny finish, and comes in a variety of colors from grey to coral-red. Travertine is also available in tile sizes for floor installations.
